The web and API maintain separate plan allowlists, and they have drifted.

- The API’s [plans.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/ad0f3f9a-0962-407f-b4e5-9d994a4a18e5/scratchpad/wt-e6/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10) accepts `free`, `pro`, `team`, and `scale`.
- The web client’s [workspace-client.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/ad0f3f9a-0962-407f-b4e5-9d994a4a18e5/scratchpad/wt-e6/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10) only recognizes `free`, `pro`, and the stale `enterprise`.

Consequently, a new `scale` plan is valid in Python but outside the web app’s closed `Plan` set, so frontend validation or response decoding rejects it. The reverse bug also exists: the web recognizes `enterprise`, which the API enum does not.

The durable fix is to make the plan contract single-source—preferably an OpenAPI or shared JSON Schema definition—and generate the TypeScript type/client from it. CI should then verify generated files are current and run a contract test comparing all accepted plan values. Gating on new high-severity `crimes` findings would provide another backstop.

The scan also found separate route drift, including `PUT` versus backend `POST` for plan changes. That would produce a 405, not this validation error, but should be corrected or eliminated through the same generated API client.
